solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Oddly, such waffle by Democrat is made unintelligible

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd-numbered positions of the next word only

blocks.note: first and third letters of the word
to waffle is to ramble on
standard abbreviation for a Democrat

explanation.surface: A politician's waffling speech turns out to be pure gibberish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled messages are jumbled so that nobody can understand them, a direct synonym for made unintelligible.

clue.text: Fare from India, not southern island nation

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter that follows it

blocks.note: a samosa is a fried pastry snack from Indian cuisine
standard abbreviation for south or southern

explanation.surface: Food from India, but not the southern style, is served in a Pacific nation.
explanation.walkthrough: India is not the NATO letter I here, simply the country whose food is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an independent island country in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Page put on line, showing official residence

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece on another stacks it above, so the first comes before the second

blocks.note: a recto is a right-hand page of a book
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A page is placed on a washing line to display an official's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Page is not a servant boy but a leaf of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a residence that goes with a church office.

clue.text: E.g. Jerry covering Tom up with horse hair

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
covering something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: Jerry is the mouse in the Tom and Jerry cartoons
a tom is a male cat, as Tom is in the cartoon
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: The cartoon mouse hides the cat under some horsehair.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is the hair grown on the upper lip.

clue.text: Long sentence poet's always put in part of book title

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another piece

blocks.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
a page is part of a book
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A poet's lengthy line keeps appearing in the title of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book title' reads as a phrase, but book belongs to the wordplay and title alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peerage is a British noble title held for the holder's lifetime only, not inherited.

clue.text: Bones of fish from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, starting from the south means reading upwards from the bottom

blocks.note: the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: Fish bones taken from the southern sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Bones looks like fish skeletons but is the nickname for a doctor, short for sawbones, as in Star Trek's Dr McCoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old slang for a surgeon, so Bones is a nickname for a medical doctor.

clue.text: Distant area Charlie goes over

indicators.note: going over suggests flipping, so the word for a charlie is turned back to front

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for area
a charlie is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie crosses over a remote patch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is not a name or the NATO letter C here but the British word for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is reserved and emotionally remote, a common synonym for distant in manner.

clue.text: Mostly oblivious to ethics, turning up nose

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from the bottom

blocks.note: amoral means without regard to morality

explanation.surface: A largely unprincipled person sticks their nose up in disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: Nose is the wine-taster's word for a smell or bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's nose is its smell, so aroma and nose are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Working hard, I must keep time, being busy

indicators.note: keeping something means holding on to it, so the preceding pieces enclose another

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the ego is the self, the I
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Toiling away, I have to keep track of the clock because I'm so busy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'Working hard, I' is the container, and time slots in after the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the go is an idiom for being constantly active, busy all the time.

clue.text: Cool cover of chimney on the house, not attached

indicators.note: a cover is the outside of something, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: to fan something is to cool it
first and last letters of the word
on the house means given free of charge

explanation.surface: A chimney cowl sits on top of a house, but it is not fixed down.
explanation.walkthrough: Cool is a verb, to fan, rather than an adjective meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free describes someone not in love or committed to anyone, so unattached.

clue.text: Noble Scot's computer not working

blocks.note: an Apple Macintosh computer
duff is British slang for broken or useless

explanation.surface: A Scottish aristocrat complains that their computer has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the noble to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Macduff is the Thane of Fife in Shakespeare's Macbeth, a Scottish nobleman who kills the tyrant.

clue.text: One's in the soup, hiding having punched crook

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a hiding is a heavy defeat, a rout
a con, short for convict, is a criminal

explanation.surface: A villain in serious trouble, in the soup, after a hiding and having thumped a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is the idiom for being in trouble, but here it is literal: a crouton floats in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried bread served floating in soup, so it is literally something in the soup.

clue.text: Neighbour inhaling oxygen roughly

indicators.note: breathing something in takes it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to abut is to lie next to, as a neighbour does
chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: The person next door breathes in some oxygen, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbour is used as a verb, to be next to, which is what abut means.
explanation.definitionFit: About and roughly are interchangeable before a number, both meaning approximately.

clue.text: Hobby that's irrational entertaining husband recently

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your home, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: pi is an irrational number
standard abbreviation for husband
lately means in recent times

explanation.surface: Someone's new pastime seems unreasonable now that they have a husband over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like an anagram signal or adjective, but it is the noun: pi, the best-known irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is stamp collecting, a classic pastime pursued for pleasure.

clue.text: At work, no spare time to take off

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being moved about and rearranged

blocks.note: all eleven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone too busy at work to find time for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Take off sounds like taking leave, which the surface sets up; here it means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is British idiom for mimicking them, which is what an impressionist does when they impersonate.

clue.text: Little bounder devoid of ecstasy and elation

indicators.note: being devoid of something means lacking it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, a small creature that bounds
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A small rogue has lost all happiness and high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder suggests an old-fashioned cad, but here it is something that bounds: a young kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy and elation are both words for great happiness, plain synonyms.

clue.text: Salt fish for fussy eater

blocks.note: a salt and a jack are both old words for a sailor
a sprat is a small sea fish

explanation.surface: Salted fish served to someone who is picky about food.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt is not seasoning but an old sailor, as in 'old salt'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat, making him the classic picky eater.

clue.text: Marxists may deplore this guy defending English left-wingers

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: a chap is a man, a guy
standard abbreviation for English
the Labour Party is Britain's main party of the left

explanation.surface: Communists might object to a man standing up for English socialists.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the British centre-left political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap labour means poorly paid workers, the exploitation Marxist thought condemns, so the description is a cryptic hint for it.

clue.text: Letting in one single goal, including defender's header

indicators.note: a header is the top, so only the first letter of the word is used
including something means taking it inside

blocks.note: a means one
a mission is a single overriding aim
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A football team concedes a goal after a defender's header.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides the abstract meanings: a single goal is an aim, and a header is a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the act of allowing someone in, as with admission to a building.

clue.text: One may hold a light tin container, drinking beer around bachelor

indicators.note: turning around a word reads it in the opposite direction
a drinker takes liquid inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: a tin is a can
a drum is a large cylindrical container
ale is a type of beer
standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A person holding a light tin container while drinking beer around an unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A light tin container' reads as one phrase, but the light belongs to the definition and the tin and container are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabrum is a branched holder for several candles, so it is something that holds lights.

clue.text: How plain cakes may be picked up

blocks.note: first, cryptic meaning: split in two words, it describes cakes without frosting
second meaning: spotted or observed

explanation.walkthrough: Picked up looks like a homophone signal but simply means spotted; read the answer as 'not iced' for the cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: If you pick up on something you notice it, and plain cakes lack icing.

clue.text: Group of waiters said to be prompt

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the sound of the word matters rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A team of restaurant staff is told to be punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: Waiters are not restaurant staff but simply people who wait, in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal to an actor to speak or move, the same as a prompt.

clue.text: Upstanding City supporter keeps on showing brains

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from bottom to top
keeping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a bra is a supporting undergarment
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A loyal football fan of City keeps showing how clever they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC; supporter is an undergarment, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebra is the plural of cerebrum, the main part of the brain.

clue.text: Light sack carried in combat

indicators.note: something carried in is held inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a set-to is a fight
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: A lightweight bag is lugged into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Light and sack both look like nouns here, but both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something is to ignite it, which is what light means as a verb.

clue.text: Powerless English playmaker in foreign team

indicators.note: without power means the letter standing for power is removed

blocks.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright, a maker of plays
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A weak English midfielder plays in a team abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Playmaker suggests a football midfielder, but means a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter Milan is an Italian football club, a team from abroad.

clue.text: Issue limited by antivirus program

indicators.note: being limited by words means sitting within their bounds, so the answer is found inside the phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A computer problem is restricted by security software.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprog is British slang for a child, and issue means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the sense of offspring or children matches sprog, informal British word for a child.

clue.text: OK after renouncing a vice

indicators.note: renouncing something means giving it up, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: OK as a reply means agreed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives the all-clear once they have given up a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins, so a classic vice.

clue.text: Designer of scale model of car better off without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the larger word sits round the piece referred to as it

blocks.note: better off means wealthier
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Someone who designs scale models of cars would be better off without the hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale model' looks like one phrase, but scale ends the definition and model starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Richter devised the Richter scale for measuring earthquake magnitude.

clue.text: Taking off top, show off scruffy garment

indicators.note: removing the top of a down word drops its first letter

blocks.note: to brag is to boast or show off

explanation.surface: Someone strips off their top to flaunt a tatty piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a worn, tattered piece of clothing.

clue.text: Kind of inquiry about my competence

blocks.note: first meaning: friendly and good-natured
second, cryptic meaning: split into three words, it asks whether I have the ability

explanation.surface: Someone asks a kind of question about whether they are good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into 'am I able' to hear the question; 'Kind of' looks like a vague phrase but kind is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means friendly and pleasant, close in sense to kind.

clue.text: Royal house party covered by Heat the wrong way

indicators.note: something covered by another thing is enclosed in it
going the wrong way means running backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: rut is the season of sexual heat in deer
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A palace party is ruined by an unexpected heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I, a royal house.

clue.text: Low-emission vehicle departs, getting permit

blocks.note: an environmentally friendly car is a green car
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly car drives off with its licence.
explanation.walkthrough: D for departs comes from railway timetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A green card is the US permit giving a foreign national permanent residence and the right to work.
